title: res.relay leaves Content-Type to the app, frames from its length argument and adds no defaultCache

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that sets no `Content-Type` and calls `res.relay(in, 5)` with a 5-byte stream makes the client receive no `Content-Type` header, `Content-Length: 5` and the 5 body bytes.
A `Content-Type` the app set before the call (for example `res.header("Content-Type", "application/x-custom")`) is sent exactly as set, with no charset or other change.

A `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding` header the app set before the call (`res.header("Content-Length", "99")`, `res.header("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")`) is dropped, and the framing comes only from the `contentLength` argument.

Headers set before the call through `res.header`, `res.append` and `res.addCookie` are sent as set, and the header list the in-memory adapter receives at commit equals those headers plus `Content-Length` when the length is sent, with no other header added by the core.

In an app with `app.defaultCache(CachePolicy.noCache())`, a response sent with `res.relay` carries no `Cache-Control`, while a `Cache-Control` the app set with `res.header` or `res.cache` before `relay` is sent as set.

Restating FR-STATIC-008 AC-5 with the change: with the default `defaultCache(null)` a JSON route and a static file without a matching pattern send no `Cache-Control`; with `defaultCache(CachePolicy.noCache())` every response that holds no `Cache-Control` at commit, error and `304` responses included, sends `Cache-Control: no-cache`, while `res.cache(noStore())`, `res.header("Cache-Control", "max-age=5")`, a matching `options.cache` pattern and a global middleware's `res.header("Cache-Control", "private")` keep their own value; a response written by `res.relay` is the one exception and never receives the `defaultCache` value.

traceLinks.notes: trace_intent=addition_site; relay header handling and defaultCache bypass
relay is a body writer beside stream that keeps the length and sets no Content-Type

requirement: The system shall make `res.relay(in, contentLength)` send only the headers the app set before the call plus the framing taken from `contentLength` — never adding or changing `Content-Type`, dropping any app-set `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` — and never apply the app's `defaultCache` policy to a relayed response, while every other response keeps the `defaultCache` rule of FR-STATIC-008.
rationale: AC-1 ← PRD-38, PRD-190, PRD-3 (design D-029); AC-2 ← PRD-38 (design D-029); AC-3 ← PRD-38 (design D-029); AC-4 ← PRD-39; AC-5 ← PRD-40, PRD-190 (design D-030); AC-6 ← PRD-40 (design D-030). Adding the app's cache policy to a relayed response would change the meaning of the upstream response, and `stream(in, contentType)` forces a `Content-Type` and drops the length, which is why decision 17 adds a separately named writer.
implementationNotes: - `relay` can reuse `DefaultResponse.startBody` with `contentType == null` (which already removes `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` and puts the length when it is non-negative), but `begin()` (`:933-938`) applies `defaultCache` whenever no `Cache-Control` is set, so relay needs a flag that skips it (code map risk R-3). FR-STATIC-008 AC-5 is expired with this requirement as successor; its other criteria stay as verified.
